patches.why: One shader module for every kernel: a single kernel a browser rejects takes the whole GPU compositor down (Safari), and Chrome's GPU watchdog loses the device (storytold/effectcraft#1590)
Safari's WebGPU refuses fxn_median_huang: its 2048-entry histogram is over WebKit's 8192-byte limit on a function's variables
A second tab restored the first tab's live project and overwrote its session snapshot (one slot per site); only the first tab keeps the session now, and the second says so
Safari writes the whole wasm heap to OPFS when given a view into it, so crash-recovery snapshots and meta were 15 MB of garbage and nothing was recovered; the bytes are copied first

The web build never autosaved: no recovery storage, and its autosave timer never fired (now_ms() is 0 on wasm), so a reload or crashed tab lost unsaved documents (storytold/photocraft#6615). Uses craft-web-recovery from the craft-libs override.

craft-web-recovery: crash-recovery copies of unsaved documents in the browser (IndexedDB, one Web Lock per tab, counted only after commit), the unload guard and download helpers; shared by every app's web save fixes, not in storytold's craft-libs yet (storytold/craft-libs#124)
The web build had no crash recovery: edits were lost on reload. Unsaved documents are copied to IndexedDB (craft-web-recovery) and reopened after a reload or crash
